verses.zh: 当希律王的时候，耶稣生在犹太的伯利恒。有几个博士从东方来到耶路撒冷，说：
verses.en: After Jesus was born in Bethlehem[NOTE:1] in Judea, in the time[NOTE:2] of King Herod,[NOTE:3] wise men[NOTE:4] from the East came to Jerusalem[NOTE:5]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map7-E2; Map8-E2; Map10-B4.

King Herod was Herod the Great, who ruled Judea (with the support of Rome) from 37 b.c. until he died in 4 b.c. He was known for his extensive building projects (including the temple in Jerusalem) and for his cruelty.
The Greek term here, sometimes transliterated into English as magi, describes a class of wise men and priests who were astrologers (L&N 32.40).
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

Or “in its rising,” referring to the astrological significance of a star in a particular portion of the sky. The term used for the “East” in v. 1 is ἀνατολαί (anatolai, a plural form that is used typically of the rising of the sun), while in vv. 2 and 9 the singular ἀνατολή (anatolē) is used. The singular is typically used of the rising of a star and as such should not normally be translated “in the east” (cf. BDAG 74 s.v. 1: “because of the sg. and the article in contrast to ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν, vs. 1, [it is] prob. not a geograph. expr. like the latter, but rather astronomical…likew. vs. 9”).

verses.zh: 「那生下来作犹太人之王的在哪里？我们在东方看见他的星，特来拜他。」
verses.en: saying, “Where is the one who is born king of the Jews? For we saw his star when it rose[NOTE:1] and have come to worship him.”
notes: See the note on King Herod in 2:1.

verses.zh: 希律王听见了，就心里不安；耶路撒冷合城的人也都不安。
verses.en: When King Herod[NOTE:1] heard this he was alarmed, and all Jerusalem[NOTE:2] with him.
notes: Here the city (Jerusalem) is put by metonymy for its inhabitants (see E. W. Bullinger, Figures of Speech, 579).

Or “and scribes of the people.” The traditional rendering of γραμματεύς (grammateus) as “scribe” does not communicate much to the modern English reader, for whom the term might mean “professional copyist,” if it means anything at all. The people referred to here were recognized experts in the law of Moses and in traditional laws and regulations. Thus “expert in the law” comes closer to the meaning for the modern reader.

verses.zh: 他就召齐了祭司长和民间的文士，问他们说：「基督当生在何处？」
verses.en: After assembling all the chief priests and experts in the law,[NOTE:1] he asked them where the Christ[NOTE:2] was to be born.
notes: See the note on Christ in 1:16.tn Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”
A quotation from Mic 5:2.

verses.zh: 他们回答说：「在犹太的伯利恒。因为有先知记着，说：
verses.en: “In Bethlehem of Judea,” they said, “for it is written this way by the prophet:

verses.zh: 犹大地的伯利恒啊，你在犹大诸城中并不是最小的；因为将来有一位君王要从你那里出来，牧养我以色列民。」
verses.en: ‘And you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah,are in no way least among the rulers of Judah,for out of you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.’”[NOTE:1]
notes: See the note on King Herod in 2:1.

verses.zh: 当下，希律暗暗地召了博士来，细问那星是甚么时候出现的，
verses.en: Then Herod[NOTE:1] privately summoned the wise men and determined from them when the star had appeared.
notes: See the note on the word “rose” in 2:2.

verses.zh: 就差他们往伯利恒去，说：「你们去仔细寻访那小孩子，寻到了就来报信，我也好去拜他。」
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] sent them to Bethlehem and said, “Go and look carefully for the child. When you find him, inform me so that I can go and worship him as well.”
notes: BDAG 815 s.v. πίπτω 1.b.α.ב has “fall down, throw oneself to the ground as a sign of devotion, before high-ranking persons or divine beings.”

verses.zh: 他们听见王的话就去了。在东方所看见的那星忽然在他们前头行，直行到小孩子的地方，就在上头停住了。
verses.en: After listening to the king they left, and once again[NOTE:1] the star they saw when it rose[NOTE:2] led them until it stopped above the place where the child was.
notes: Frankincense refers to the aromatic resin of certain trees, used as a sweet-smelling incense (L&N 6.212).

Myrrh consisted of the aromatic resin of certain shrubs (L&N 6.208). It was widely used in the ancient Near East by the Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans as perfume, as incense, and for medicinal purposes (W. Michaelis, TDNT 7:457). It was also used in preparing a corpse for burial (cf. John 19:39).

verses.zh: 他们看见那星，就大大地欢喜；
verses.en: When they saw the star they shouted joyfully.[NOTE:1]
notes: See the note on King Herod in 2:1.

verses.zh: 进了房子，看见小孩子和他母亲马利亚，就俯伏拜那小孩子，揭开宝盒，拿黄金、乳香、没药为礼物献给他。
verses.en: As they came into the house and saw the child with Mary his mother, they bowed down[NOTE:1] and worshiped him. They opened their treasure boxes and gave him gifts of gold, frankincense,[NOTE:2] and myrrh.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “the angel of the Lord.” See the note on the word “Lord” in 1:20.
See the note on King Herod in 2:1. Herod the Great was particularly ruthless regarding the succession to his throne.
The feminine singular genitive noun νυκτός (nuktos, “night”) indicates the time during which the action of the main verb takes place (ExSyn 124).

verses.zh: 博士因为在梦中被主指示不要回去见希律，就从别的路回本地去了。
verses.en: After being warned in a dream not to return to Herod,[NOTE:1] they went back by another route to their own country.
notes: See the note on King Herod in 2:1.

verses.zh: 他们去后，有主的使者向约瑟梦中显现，说：「起来！带着小孩子同他母亲逃往埃及，住在那里，等我吩咐你；因为希律必寻找小孩子，要除灭他。」
verses.en: After they had gone, an[NOTE:1] angel of the Lord[NOTE:2] appeared to Joseph in a dream and said, “Get up, take the child and his mother and flee to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you, for Herod[NOTE:3] is going to look for the child to kill him.”
notes: A quotation from Hos 11:1.
See the note on King Herod in 2:1. Note the fulfillment of the prophecy given by the angel in 2:13.
Or “soldiers.”

verses.zh: 约瑟就起来，夜间带着小孩子和他母亲往埃及去，
verses.en: Then he got up, took the child and his mother during[NOTE:1] the night, and went to Egypt.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map7-E2; Map8-E2; Map10-B4.

verses.zh: 住在那里，直到希律死了。这是要应验主藉先知所说的话，说：「我从埃及召出我的儿子来。」
verses.en: He stayed there until Herod[NOTE:1] died. In this way what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet was fulfilled: “I called my Son out of Egypt.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The LXX of Jer 38:15 (31:15 ET) has “lamentation, weeping, and loud wailing”; most later mss (C D L W Γ Δ 0233 ƒ13 33 565 579 700 1241 1424 M) have a quotation in Matthew which conforms to that of the LXX (θρῆνος καὶ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὀδυρμός; thrēnos kai klauthmos kai odurmos). But such assimilations were routine among the scribes; as such, they typically should be discounted because they are both predictable and motivated. The shorter reading, without “lamentation and,” is thus to be preferred, especially since it cannot easily be accounted for unless it is the reading that gave rise to the other reading. Further, it is found in the better mss along with a good cross-section of other witnesses (א B Z 0250 ƒ1 lat co).
A quotation from Jer 31:15.

verses.zh: 希律见自己被博士愚弄，就大大发怒，差人将伯利恒城里并四境所有的男孩，照着他向博士仔细查问的时候，凡两岁以里的，都杀尽了。
verses.en: When Herod[NOTE:1] saw that he had been tricked by the wise men, he became enraged. He sent men[NOTE:2] to kill all the children in Bethlehem[NOTE:3] and throughout the surrounding region from the age of two and under, according to the time he had learned from the wise men.
notes: See the note on King Herod in 2:1. When Herod the Great died in 4 b.c., his kingdom was divided up among his three sons: Archelaus, who ruled over Judea (where Bethlehem was located, v. 22); Philip, who became tetrarch of Iturea and Trachonitis (cf. Luke 3:1); and Antipas, who became tetrarch of Galilee.
Or “the angel of the Lord.” See the note on the word “Lord” in 1:20.
Archelaus took after his father Herod the Great in terms of cruelty and ruthlessness, so Joseph was afraid to go there. After further direction in a dream, he went instead to Galilee.

verses.zh: 这就应了先知耶利米的话，说：
verses.en: Then what was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled:

verses.zh: 在拉玛听见号啕大哭的声音，是拉结哭她儿女，不肯受安慰，因为他们都不在了。
verses.en: “A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and loud wailing,[NOTE:1] Rachel weeping for her children, and she did not want to be comforted, because they were[NOTE:2] gone.”[NOTE:3]
notes: See the note on King Herod in 2:1.

For location see Map1-D3; Map2-C2; Map3-D5; Map4-C1; Map5-G3.sn Nazareth was a very small village in the region of Galilee (Galilee lay north of Samaria and Judea). The town was located about 15 mi (25 km) west of the southern edge of the Sea of Galilee. According to Luke 1:26, Mary was living in Nazareth when the birth of Jesus was announced to her.

There is no expressed subject of the third person singular verb here; the pronoun “he” is implied. Instead of this pronoun the referent “Jesus” has been supplied in the text to clarify to whom this statement refers.

verses.zh: 希律死了以后，有主的使者在埃及向约瑟梦中显现，说：
verses.en: After Herod[NOTE:1] had died, an[NOTE:2] angel of the Lord[NOTE:3] appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt
notes: The Greek could be indirect discourse (as in the text), or direct discourse (“he will be called a Nazarene”). Judging by the difficulty of finding OT quotations (as implied in the plural “prophets”) to match the wording here, it appears that the author was using a current expression of scorn that conceptually (but not verbally) found its roots in the OT.

verses.zh: 「起来！带着小孩子和他母亲往以色列地去，因为要害小孩子性命的人已经死了。」
verses.en: saying, “Get up, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel, for those who were seeking the child’s life are dead.”

verses.zh: 约瑟就起来，把小孩子和他母亲带到以色列地去；
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] he got up and took the child and his mother and returned to the land of Israel.

verses.zh: 只因听见亚基老接着他父亲希律作了犹太王，就怕往那里去，又在梦中被主指示，便往加利利境内去了，
verses.en: But when he heard that Archelaus[NOTE:1] was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod,[NOTE:2] he was afraid to go there. After being warned in a dream, he went to the regions of Galilee.

verses.zh: 到了一座城，名叫拿撒勒，就住在那里。这是要应验先知所说，他将称为拿撒勒人的话了。
verses.en: He came to a town called Nazareth[NOTE:1] and lived there. Then what had been spoken by the prophets was fulfilled, that Jesus[NOTE:2] would be called a Nazarene.[NOTE:3]
